newsitem.title: UK: UK minister sees balanced rebound, no runaway boom.
newsitem.headline: UK minister sees balanced rebound, no runaway boom.

text.p: Britain is enjoying a balanced economic recovery, not a runaway boom, junior Treasury minister Phillip Oppenheim said on Thursday.

Oppenheim was asked by BBC radio whether brisk retail sales over Christmas reinforced Bank of England governor Eddie George's warning, in an interview on Tuesday with France's Le Figaro newspaper, that British interest rates may need to rise.
"I don't think a good Christmas makes an uncontrollable boom. What we now have is a balanced recovery.

"We have very strong export growth, we have industry doing generally very well and consumers are now benefiting too as a result of that -- as we've seen by the good sales figures over Christmas," Oppenheim replied.

He said if and when Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke made any decisions on interest rates he would do so in the interest of the economy. "And ultimately it's strong economies that win elections," Oppenheim added.
Clarke last raised interest rates to six percent from 5.75 percent on October 30.
